analyst_view.overall: League leaders Arsenal (24 points, eight wins in nine) host promoted Hull, who are 11th and winless in six league games (four draws). Arteta confirmed Ezri Konsa is fine after being taken off as a precaution in Prague, Ben White is back, and Saliba is in contention, so only Saka (thigh/quad, out until after the break) and the suspended Dowman are missing. Hull have seven players injured, including goalkeeper Jack Butland, who one report says could still play, and Matt Crooks is suspended.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. Arsenal control games rather than run up scores, and Saka's absence removes their main creator. Hull have scored only 11 in nine league games and draw a lot. Sergej Jakirovic admits he found no weakness in Arsenal and wants to make the game uncomfortable for them, which points to a low-scoring match.

corners.text: The numbers say about 10 corners, most of them Arsenal's. Arteta wants his side to attack from the start, and Hull, with seven players injured, are likely to sit deep. That points to Arsenal pinning them back and forcing plenty of blocked crosses and set pieces.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, mostly from Hull. Hull lose their combative midfielder Matt Crooks to suspension, and a one-sided game in which Arsenal keep the ball usually produces few flashpoints. Farai Hallam referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots. A deep Hull block suits a high Arsenal shot count, and Arsenal's defence is close to full strength. Missing Saka pulls the other way, so the model's figure looks about right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. Without Saka, Arsenal lose their main source of chances from the right, and a packed Hull defence should block plenty. Hull rarely test goalkeepers away from home.
